subject: Data retention & deletion SLAs — follow-up and clarifications
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@amayahealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Data retention / deletion SLA questions + next steps

Hi Sanjay / Lina —

Thanks again for taking the time today — great convo with the Amaya team. Quick recap and next steps on the items we said we'd follow up on: 

1) SOC 2 / HIPAA: You asked whether Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and if we can provide evidence and a BAA for HIPAA workloads. We'll pull the latest SOC 2 report and confirm the BAA process.

2) Vendor security questionnaire: I attached the vendor security questionnaire you mentioned (Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.pdf). Please let us know if you prefer we fill and return it via DocuSign or upload to your procurement portal.

3) Data retention / deletion SLAs (clarifications needed): On the call you raised several specifics we wanted to confirm back on: 
   - Primary customer data deletion SLA (requested by customer) — is immediate purge required, or acceptable to have a 30-day deletion window?
   - Backups: how long are backups retained, and what is the SLA for removing customer data from backups after a deletion request?
   - Log retention: default log retention vs options for longer retention for audit purposes.

Next steps from Redwood:
- We'll answer the retention/backups/logs questions with proposed SLAs and clarify deletion behaviors (soft delete vs hard purge) and backup retention/purge windows.
- I'll loop in Neha (security/compliance lead) and Rishi (product infra) to confirm specifics and provide language you can share with procurement.
- We'll start the security questionnaire and share SOC2/BAA materials via secure link.

Proposed cadence: I'll send a written summary with the proposed SLAs by EOD tomorrow, and we can schedule a short call with our security engineer if you want deeper technical detail.

Attachments: Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (stub)

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@amayahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Torres <lina.torres@amayahealth.com>, procurement@amayahealth.com
Date: 2026-08-21T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Data retention / deletion SLA questions + next steps

Marissa —

Appreciate the quick recap. A few answers and clarifications from Amaya: 

- SOC 2 / HIPAA: We require SOC 2 Type II evidence for production customers. HIPAA — we will need a signed BAA before any PHI production data is sent. Please confirm you have an existing BAA template and provide next steps.

- Deletion SLA: For our use case, we need the ability to request deletion of customer data with a maximum of 30 days for primary data to be removed from active systems. For GDPR subject access requests, we prefer same-day soft-delete and 30 days max for full removal where technically feasible.

- Backups: Our procurement team prefers backups to be retained no longer than 12 months. Critically, we need a clear policy on when backups that contain deleted customer data will be purged — procurement is comfortable with a maximum of 60 days after a deletion request for backup purge, provided the customer is informed.

- Logs: Default retention of 90 days is acceptable for many of our services, but we may need options for extended retention (up to 24 months) for certain audit trails. Would Redwood support configurable log retention windows per account?

I've attached our internal retention summary (Amaya_Retention_Requirements.xlsx) for reference.

If you can confirm these points in writing, procurement will move forward on the security questionnaire and BAA. We're open to a short follow-up call next week with your security team.

Thanks —
Sanjay Rao
Director of IT Security | Amaya Health
sanjay@amayahealth.com | +1 212-555-0123

Date: 2026-08-21T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call: Data retention / deletion SLA questions + next steps (internal)

Marissa / Rishi —

Quick internal note after reading Sanjay's replies and the Amaya requirements attachment:

Summary of asks:
- SOC 2 Type II evidence and BAA required (procurement will not proceed without).
- Deletion SLA: customer requests — target 30 days for primary data; GDPR requests expect faster (soft-delete same-day where possible).
- Backups: retention target 12 months; purge of customer data from backups within 60 days of deletion request.
- Logs: default 90 days, with configurable extensions up to 24 months.

What we can commit to today (draft):
- Primary data deletion: Redwood supports account-level deletion requests. Standard SLA: 30 calendar days to remove data from active/primary systems. For GDPR subject requests, we will perform a soft-delete within 24 hours and prioritize full removal within 30 days.
- Backups: Redwood retains encrypted backups for 12 months by default. For deletion requests, we'll schedule backup purges on a 60-day retention purge window; note that immediate purging from immutable backup media may require coordination and we should document the exact process in the BAA/contract.
- Logs: Default retention 90 days. We can offer configurable log retention up to 24 months at account provisioning; this may incur additional cost.

Open questions / risks to escalate:
1) Immediate purge from backups: some of our backup systems are designed for write-once retention; full purge may require rekeying or retention-lifecycle processes and could take us longer than 60 days in some environments. Need confirmation from infra (Rishi) on which storage/backups we can guarantee a 60-day purge.
2) HIPAA / BAA: Legal to confirm our standard BAA template and if any redlines from Amaya are typical.

Suggested next steps (internal):
- Rishi: confirm backup purge capabilities and any edge cases where 60 days may not be met.
- Legal: prepare BAA and SOC2 share link. I'll draft the security questionnaire answers for the vendor doc and share for review.

If those are agreeable, Marissa should respond to Sanjay with the proposed SLA language, confirm we'll share SOC2 link & BAA, and propose a 30-minute call with our security engineer next week.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@amayahealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, procurement@amayahealth.com
Date: 2026-08-22T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Data retention / deletion SLA questions + next steps

Hi Sanjay / Lina / procurement —

Thanks for the details and the attachment. Following internal confirmation, here are the proposed commitments from Redwood to help procurement move forward: 

1) SOC 2 / BAA: We'll share a secure link to our latest SOC 2 Type II report and a standard BAA template. Please review and flag any redlines — our legal team can iterate as needed. SOC2 link: https://redwood-drive.example.com/share/secure/SOC2-TypeII

2) Deletion SLA (primary data): Redwood will process customer-initiated deletion requests with a standard SLA of 30 calendar days to remove data from active/primary systems. For GDPR subject access/deletion requests, we will perform a soft-delete within 24 hours and prioritize full removal within 30 days where technically feasible.

3) Backups: Redwood retains encrypted backups for 12 months by default. For deletion requests, Redwood will schedule backup purges with a target window of 60 days to remove customer data from backups. Note: in rare cases involving immutable retention or third-party archival systems, we may need to coordinate with procurement/ops to document the exact purge process; we'll call those out in the contract.

4) Logs: Default log retention is 90 days. We support configurable retention windows up to 24 months on request; extended retention may require an addendum and additional cost.

Next steps:
- I'll attach the completed vendor questionnaire (Redwood_Security_Questionnaire_Completed.pdf) and upload SOC2/BAA via secure link.
- Neha will join a short call next week to walk your security team through any technical details; what times are good for you Tue/Wed morning PST?
- If procurement is happy with the above, please confirm and we can circulate a redline-ready BAA/contract.

Attachments: Redwood_Security_Questionnaire_Completed.pdf

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
